content: 1. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole, may elevate plasma hormone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (both intrauterine and oral forms) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of linagliptin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 7. Drospirenone reduces the effects of liraglutide by increasing pH and altering passive renal tubular reabsorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Drospirenone and lisinopril may synergistically increase the risk of hyperkalemia. Close monitoring is advised. 9. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of lomitapide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Drospirenone increases the levels of lomitapide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to its starting dose and monitor for arrhythmias and QT interval changes. 13. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response. Higher growth hormone doses may be required. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 14. Drospirenone decreases the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing IGF-1 response. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 15. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing contraceptive efficacy. 16. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Drospirenone and lornoxicam both increase serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 18. Losartan and drospirenone both increase serum potassium levels. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of losartan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during coadministration. 21. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of macimorelin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Drospirenone increases magnesium levels (chloride, citrate, hydroxide, oxide, sulfate) by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Maitake increases the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of marijuana by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and drospirenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding may occur. 29. Drospirenone and meclofenamate both increase serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 31. Drospirenone and mefenamic acid both increase serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 33. Drospirenone and meloxicam both increase serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 34. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of mestranol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 35. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while metaproterenol decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 36. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of metaxalone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 37. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drospirenone also decreases the effects of metformin through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of methadone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 39. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while methyclothiazide decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 40. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of methylergonovine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while metolazone decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 43. Metoprolol and drospirenone both increase serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 44. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of metyrapone through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Estrogen therapy, including oral contraceptives, may reduce the therapeutic response to metyrapone. 46. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of miconazole oral by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 48. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of midazolam (oral and intranasal) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 50. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 51. Mifepristone decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol and drospirenone through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 53. Mineral oil decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 54. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Drospirenone increases the effects of minoxidil through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 56. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 57. Mitotane decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 58. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of modafinil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 59. Moexipril and drospirenone may synergistically increase the risk of hyperkalemia. Close monitoring is advised. 60. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinylestradiol by competing for plasma protein binding. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates, necessitating dose adjustments of other BCRP substrates. 61. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of montelukast by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
